questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the molarity of a solution containing 5 g of NaOH dissolved in the product of $\mathrm{H}_2-\mathrm{O}_2$ fuel cell operated at 1 A current for 595.1 hours. (Assume $\mathrm{F}=96500 \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{mol}$ of electron and molecular weight of NaOH as $\left.40 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right)$.
questions.solution:
The overall reaction of $\mathrm{H}_2-$$\mathrm{O}_2$ fuel is,
$2 $$\mathrm{H}_2+$$\mathrm{O}_2$ \longrightarrow 2 $\mathrm{H}_2 $$\mathrm{O}$$
Thus $4 $\mathrm{ F}=$4 \times 96500 $\mathrm{C}$ produce water $=2 $$\mathrm{ mol}=$$36 $$\mathrm{ g}$$\begin{aligned}
$$\text{ Charge actually passed }$$ & =i \times t \\
& =1 \times 595.1 \times 60 \times 60 \\
& =2142360 $$\mathrm{C}$$
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \therefore $$\text{ Water produced }=$$\frac{36}{4 \times 96500}$ \times 2142360 \\
& \cong 200 $\mathrm{ g} $$\text{ or }$$ 200 $$\mathrm{ mL}$$ \\
& \therefore $\text{ Molarity$ of } $$\mathrm{NaOH} \text{ solution }=$$\frac{5}{40}$ \times $\frac{1}{200}$ \times 1000 \\
& =0.625 $\mathrm{M}$
\end{aligned}

questions.q:
The conductivity of a weak acid HA of concentration $0.001 \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}$ is $2.0 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~cm}^{-1}$.
If $\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{{}^{\circ}}(\mathrm{HA})=190 \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~cm}^2 \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$, the ionization constant $\left(\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}\right) of \mathrm{HA}$ is equal to _______ x $10^{-6}$.
questions.solution:
$\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}=1000 \times \frac{\mathrm{K}}{\mathrm{M}}$
$=1000 \times \frac{2 \times 10^{-5}}{0.001}=20 \mathrm{ S} \mathrm{ cm}^2 \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$
$\Rightarrow \alpha=\frac{\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}^{{}^{\circ}}}=\frac{20}{190}= \left(\frac{2}{19}\right)
$\underset{0.001(1-$\alpha)}{\mathrm{HA}}$\rightleftharpoons \underset{0.001 \alpha$}{\mathrm{H}^{+}}$+\underset{0.001 \alpha$}{\mathrm{A}^{-}}$
K_${\mathrm{a}}$=0.001$\left(\frac{\alpha^2}{1-\alpha}\right)=\frac{0.001 \times\left(\frac{2}{19}\right)^2}{1-\left(\frac{2}{19}\right)}
$=12.3 $\times10^{-6}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
${E}_{1}, {E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{3}$ are the emf of the following three galvanic cells respectively

(i) $Zn \left(s\right)\left|{Zn}^{2 +} \left(0 . 1M\right)\right|\left|{Cu}^{2 +}\left(1M\right)\right|$ Cu$\left($ s\right)$

(ii) $Zn $\left(s\right)\left|{Zn}^{2 +} \left(1M\right)\right|\left|{Cu}^{2 +}\left(1M\right)\right|Cu\left(s\right)$

(iii) $Zn \left(s\right)\left|{Zn}^{2 +} \left(1M\right)\right| \left|{Cu}^{2 +}\left(0 . 1M\right)\right|$ Cu$\left($ s\right)$

Which of the following is true?

$
questions.solution:
Key-idea

Use Nernst equation, i.e.

$E\left(emf\right) = E{°}_{cell} - \dfrac{0 . 0591}{2}log\dfrac{\left[{Zn}^{2 +}\right]}{\left[{Cu}^{2 +}\right]}$

For reaction $\left(i\right)$

${E}_{1} = E{°}_{\left(cell\right)} - \dfrac{0 . 0591}{2}log\dfrac{0 . 1}{1}$

${E}_{1} = E{°}_{\left(cell\right)} + \dfrac{0 . 0591}{2}$

For reaction $\left(ii\right)$

${E}_{2} = E{°}_{\left(cell\right)} - \dfrac{0 . 0591}{2}log\dfrac{1}{1} = 0$

${E}_{2} = E{°}_{\left(cell\right)}$

For reaction $\left(iii\right)$

${E}_{3} = E{°}_{\left(cell\right)} - \dfrac{0 . 0591}{2}log\dfrac{1}{0 . 1}$

${E}_{3} = E{°}_{\left(cell\right)} - \dfrac{0 . 0591}{2}$

Hence, ${E}_{1} > {E}_{2} > {E}_{3}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What time in sec is required for depositing all the silver present in $125ml$ of $1M{AgNO}_{3}$ solution by passing a current of $241. 25$ A (Given $1F = 96500C$)
questions.solution:
Given, $125ml$ of $1M{AgNO}_{3}$

which is equal to $13. 5g$ of $Ag$

$∵ 1000ml$ of ${AgNO}_{3} = 108g$ of $Ag$

$∴ 125ml$ of ${AgNO}_{3} = \dfrac{108 \times 125}{1000} = 13. 5g$

Also, $∵ 108g$ of $Ag$ is deposited by $= 96500C$

$∴ 13. 5g$ of $Ag$ is deposited by $= \dfrac{96500 \times 13. 5}{108} = 12062. 5C$

$∵ Q = it$

$∴ t$ (time) $= Q / i = \dfrac{12062. 50}{241. 25}, t = 50sec$

questions.q: $0. 5F$ of electricity is passed through $500mL$ of copper sulphate solution. The amount of copper which can be deposited will be
questions.solution:
${Cu}^{2 +} + 2e^{-} ⟶ Cu... \left(i\right)$

According to Faraday's first law, when an electric current is passed through an electrolyte, amount of substance deposited is directly proportional to the quantity of electric charge passed through the electrolyte.

$∵ 1mol$ of $63. 5g$ of $Cu$ is obtained by passing $2F$ of electricity.

Mass of $Cu$ obtained by passing $1F$ of electricity $= \dfrac{63. 5}{2}$ g$

$∴$ Mass of $Cu$ obtained by passing 0. 5F$ of electricity
$= \dfrac{63. 5}{2} \times0. 5 = 15. 80g$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a reaction, $A + B^{2 +} ⟶ B + A^{2 +}$, at ${25}^{0}CE^{0} = 0. 2955V$. The value of ${K}_{eq}$ is
questions.solution:
Given that,

For a reaction,&

$A + B^{2 +} ⟶ B + A^{2 +}, E ° = 0. 2955V$

$T = {25}^{°}C, ⇒ T = 298Kn = 2$

Using Nernst equation,

$E ° = \dfrac{2. 303RT}{nF}{logk}_{eq}$

$E ° = \dfrac{0. 0591}{n}{logk}_{eq} \left(at{25}^{o}C\right)$

$⇒ 0. 2955 = \dfrac{0. 0591}{2}$ log{k}_{eq}$

${k}_{eq} = {10}^{10}$

Therefore, the value of ${K}_{eq}$ is ${10}^{10}$.

$

$∵$ Reaction between $Fe$ and $HCl$ is as follows

$Fe + 2HCl ⟶ \mathop{FeCl2}_{( + 2 )} + {H}_{2}$ on reaction

$n$(moles of $Fe$) $= n$ (moles of $HCl$)

$n ( Fe ) =$ Normality $( HCl ) \times$ Volume of $HCl$

$n\left(Fe\right) = \dfrac{0. 4 \times 500}{1000} = 0. 2moles$
